name: San Marino
summary: Succession law is not codified, and children and the spouse are protected by a reserved share whose size was not confirmed. The Hague Trusts Convention is in force and San Marino has its own trust law. Foundations were not confirmed.
reserved_share: A reserved part (portio debita) exists for legitimate heirs under San Marino's common-law rules, with spouse rights in intestacy under Law 49/1986 (usufruct of the whole estate plus a child-sized share when there are children). Sizes of the reserve were not confirmed.
foreign_law_note: San Marino private international law on succession was not found. Not under the EU Regulation.
trust_note: The Hague Trusts Convention is in force since 1 August 2006 (HCCH table: accession 28 April 2005). San Marino has its own trust statute (a secondary source says domestic trusts are governed by San Marino law with a specialised court). Fiduciary contracts also exist. The existence and scope of a foundation law were not confirmed; the entry 'limited' is a placeholder.
open_questions: Size of the reserve and the conflict rule for succession were not found.
Trust statute citation (law number and date) was not read.
Foundations: no source found; 'limited' is not backed by a source.
Trust/foundation availability marked unclear: no statute was found, which does not show that none exists.
